speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I'm Dr. Agent. You're an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche and unusual physical features; can you describe exactly what those physical features look like and do you have a history of fractures or bone pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of labial fusion at birth, maternal hirsutism, severe acne, and bone fractures in an adolescent with delayed menarche is highly concerning for Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH). To confirm this, I need to see the imaging of your skeletal abnormalities. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_XRay_and_Bone_Density_Scan. Do you also have a family history of similar symptoms or infertility?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (Non-classic/Adult-onset type with virilization at birth).

The combination of delayed menarche, severe acne, bone fractures, and specific genital anomalies (labial fusion, clitoromegaly) strongly suggests a form of CAH, possibly due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency. While I have requested the skeletal imaging, do you have any known family history of endocrine disorders or infertility, and have any blood tests been done to check your cortisol and androgen levels?
